title: Chisle: fewer tokens than caveman and ponytail, no accuracy lost
excerpt: The Claude Code plugin that makes coding answers about half as long. Terse persona + tool-output compressor + context diet.
content_html:
Built for Claude Code. One command, thirteen agents.
Answers about half as long, same pass rate as the bare model. Every number traces to a committed transcript.

  • Terse persona
  • Output compressor
  • Context diet
  • Zero dependencies
  • No network calls
  • MIT licensed

Run this. Done.

npx chisle
# auto-detects all 13 agents · zero deps · zero network calls
# preview: npx chisle --dry-run   undo: npx chisle --uninstall

Get started

Cut the bill in under a minute

One command installs the persona, the compressor hook and the context-diet rules into every agent it finds. Nothing to configure, nothing to call home.

Full install guide →

  1. Install

    Auto-detects all 13 agents.

  2. Open your agent as usual

    The ruleset loads once on a new session (~900 tokens), then a ~50-token reminder per turn keeps it alive through compaction. Tool output gets compressed before the model reads it, and the statusline shows what was actually elided.

    [CHISLE] ⇣9k tok

  3. Update, or switch it off

    update

    npx chisle@latest --update

    persona off

    "stop chisle"

    remove all

    npx chisle --uninstall

    Plain npx chisle skips what is already installed, so updates need @latest --update.

Runs where you work

Thirteen agents, one install

Full coverage where the agent exposes hooks. Elsewhere the persona ships as a generated rule file and stays always on, and npx chisle mcp wrap compresses MCP tool output.

Features

One plugin, three levers

Other token savers only make the model write less. Tool output is the bigger bill, 67.5% of a session, and it re-bills every turn.

How the model writes

Terse persona

Senior-dev voice: fragments over sentences, YAGNI-first code, reuse before new code. One mode, no dials. Commits and security warnings stay verbose on purpose.

What survives into context

Output compressor

A post-tool hook shrinks tool results before the model reads them: ANSI scrub, head + tail elide with error-line salvage, same-session dedup. Never touches Read, Edit, or Write. Runs on Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode and Copilot CLI, and on the MCP servers of any agent via npx chisle mcp wrap.

What gets read at all

Context diet

Rules that teach the model to fetch the slice, not the file: grep first, sliced reads, filter at the source, never re-read what's already in context.

Live savings statusline

A ⇣9k tok badge showing chars actually elided. Before v2.0.0 it counted compressions the harness went on to reject. That is fixed, and it now records only what is really applied.

Tested where it matters

The compressor is where a bug corrupts files, so it's covered by the test suite, with a hard allowlist.

Easy off-switch

"stop chisle" for the persona, CHISLE_COMPRESS=0 for the hook, npx chisle --uninstall for everything.

How it works

Three hooks, one session

Two hooks shape what the model writes. The third shrinks what it reads, and that one is a loop.

Hover a hook, in the diagram or below it.

Tool output is billed again on everylater request in the session, so shrinking it once pays repeatedly. The compressor rebuilds its result into the tool's own response shape; returning a bare string gets the replacement rejected, which is exactly the bug that made this axis a no-op before v2.0.0.

The compressor, live

400 lines of build output. Two matter.

Tool results re-bill on every later turn. The compressor keeps the head, the tail, and any error or warning lines from the middle. The rest never reaches the model.

Deterministic: no LLM calls, no network, no dependencies. Allowlist: Bash, Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch, Grep, Glob, mcp__*. Never Read/Edit/Write. Successful calls only: Claude Code sends a failed command to PostToolUseFailure, which no hook can rewrite, and truncates that output itself.

Compare

Same prompt. Same model. Real transcripts.

Pick a task and an arm. Both panels are the verbatim committed output from the benchmark run, not a mock-up written for this page. The arms differ only in the injected system prompt.

“Add a cache layer for our user profile API responses. Show the code.”

bare model177 answer tok · 8 lines

I need more context to help you add a cache layer. Could you clarify:

  1. What framework/language is your API built with? (e.g., Node.js/Express, Python/FastAPI, Go, etc.)
  2. Do you have existing code I should look at, or is this a new project?
  3. What caching backend do you prefer? (e.g., Redis, in-memory, Node's built-in, etc.)
  4. Cache strategy: TTL (time-to-live), invalidation approach, etc.?

If you have existing code, you can share the file path or paste it, and I'll add caching to it. Otherwise, I can show you a complete example once I know your tech stack.

25% · 44 answer tok · 1 lines

No project here—/tmp isn't a git repo. Point me to the code, or should I show a minimal cache pattern example (in-memory, Redis, or decorator)?

basis: measured2026-11-06 re-run, default suite seed 1, Haiku 4.5, tools off, isolated configs; arms differ only in the injected system prompt. Percentages are answer tokens against the bare model's. Read this one carefully: the prompt ships with no codebase attached, so every arm, the bare model included, asks for the stack instead of writing a cache. This cell measures how briefly each one asks, not how much code it writes. Browse every cell in benchmarks/results/raw-nov/default-s1.

The efficiency ladder

Seven rungs, before a line gets written

The agent stops at the first rung that holds, and the ladder runs after reading the problem, never instead of it. Hover to pause.

Every rung exits the same way: ship it, then say what was skipped and when to add it, so “later” doesn't quietly become “never”. Lazy about the solution, never about the reading. Trust-boundary validation, data-loss handling, security and accessibility are never on the chopping block.

Benchmarks

The lowest bill, measured

Same model, same prompts, one difference: the injected ruleset. Billed output tokens as a share of the bare model, every arm in one run on Claude Code + Haiku 4.5. Raw transcripts and the runner ship in the repo.

chisle

chisle 3.8.1

caveman

ponytail

bare model

Leanest on every row

% of the bare model, current Chisle (ruleset unchanged since 3.9) on Haiku 4.5, 25 live prompts in one run. On Sonnet 5.5, Chisle bills 57% of the bare model.

metriccavemanponytailchisle
billed tokens · Claude Code87%90%71%
answer length · Claude Code59%62%55%
answer lines · Claude Code55%60%45%

Correctness: shorter, not wronger

Auto-graded, no judge model. Neither gap is significant (Fisher p = 0.498, 0.738).

suitebare modelchisle
maths + coding, 52 problems × 3 seeds154 / 156156 / 156
real repos, hidden tests, 7 fixtures × 6 seeds36 / 4238 / 42

Plus the input side: the compressor trims ~46% off every oversized tool output before it re-enters context. Chisle began as a merge of caveman and ponytail; their MIT notices are in the repo's NOTICE file.

FAQ

Questions, answered tersely

No. Terse ≠ incomplete. The rules cut words around the facts, never the facts: the fix, the gotcha, the caveat all stay. On 156 auto-graded maths and coding problems Chisle scored 156/156, the bare model 154/156; on 42 agentic repo runs with hidden tests, 38 vs 36.

Stop paying for filler. Start shipping.

MIT licensed, built in the open. Land a PR, or file an issue good enough to fix itself, and you are credited in the repo.

Free and MIT, but every benchmark run costs real API money. A coffee keeps them coming.

Co-engineered with Claude, Codex & Antigravity · descended from caveman & ponytail

开始使用

Cut the bill in under a minute

One command installs the persona, the compressor hook and the context-diet rules into every agent it finds. Nothing to configure, nothing to call home.

Full install guide →

  1. InstallAuto-detects all 13 agents.
  2. Open your agent as usualThe ruleset loads once on a new session (~900 tokens), then a ~50-token reminder per turn keeps it alive through compaction. Tool output gets compressed before the model reads it, and the statusline shows what was actually elided.[CHISLE] ⇣9k tok
  3. Update, or switch it offupdatenpx chisle@latest --updatepersona off"stop chisle"remove allnpx chisle --uninstallPlain npx chisle skips what is already installed, so updates need @latest --update.

Runs where you work

Thirteen agents, one install

Full coverage where the agent exposes hooks. Elsewhere the persona ships as a generated rule file and stays always on, and npx chisle mcp wrap compresses MCP tool output.

特征

One plugin, three levers

Other token savers only make the model write less. Tool output is the bigger bill, 67.5% of a session, and it re-bills every turn.

How the model writes

Terse persona

Senior-dev voice: fragments over sentences, YAGNI-first code, reuse before new code. One mode, no dials. Commits and security warnings stay verbose on purpose.

What survives into context

Output compressor

A post-tool hook shrinks tool results before the model reads them: ANSI scrub, head + tail elide with error-line salvage, same-session dedup. Never touches Read, Edit, or Write. Runs on Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode and Copilot CLI, and on the MCP servers of any agent via npx chisle mcp wrap.

What gets read at all

Context diet

Rules that teach the model to fetch the slice, not the file: grep first, sliced reads, filter at the source, never re-read what's already in context.

Live savings statusline

A ⇣9k tok badge showing chars actually elided. Before v2.0.0 it counted compressions the harness went on to reject. That is fixed, and it now records only what is really applied.

Tested where it matters

The compressor is where a bug corrupts files, so it's covered by the test suite, with a hard allowlist.

Easy off-switch

"stop chisle" for the persona, CHISLE_COMPRESS=0 for the hook, npx chisle --uninstall for everything.

它是如何运作的

Three hooks, one session

Two hooks shape what the model writes. The third shrinks what it reads, and that one is a loop.

SessionStart~900 tok · new sessions onlyUserPromptSubmit~50 tok · every turnmodelterser proseYAGNI-first codewritesBash · Grep · WebFetch · mcp__*callsPostToolUsescrub → elide → dedupcompressed, in the tool's own shapeRead · Editnever touched

Hover a hook, in the diagram or below it.

Tool output is billed again on everylater request in the session, so shrinking it once pays repeatedly. The compressor rebuilds its result into the tool's own response shape; returning a bare string gets the replacement rejected, which is exactly the bug that made this axis a no-op before v2.0.0.

The compressor, live

400 lines of build output. Two matter.

Tool results re-bill on every later turn. The compressor keeps the head, the tail, and any error or warning lines from the middle. The rest never reaches the model.

Deterministic: no LLM calls, no network, no dependencies. Allowlist: Bash, Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch, Grep, Glob, mcp__*. Never Read/Edit/Write. Successful calls only: Claude Code sends a failed command to PostToolUseFailure, which no hook can rewrite, and truncates that output itself.
